_comment: Design tokens — THE single source for every color and type role in the product. DOCUMENT palette (paper, ink, navy, accent, panel, slate=dim, warning=danger, caution=warn, ok, rule) is AUTHENTIC STYLE v2.1 (Rob, 6 Sep 2026; specimen at docs/brand/authentic-style-specimen.pdf): every generated PDF and the kneeboard derive from it via missiongen/authentic.py. The sys_* and role_* keys are the SITE (Apple HIG, unchanged). Change here, regenerate, ship.
_source: Flightline Technical kit · DESIGN.md rev alpha · derived from MIL-STD-38784B / MIL-STD-3001 conventions
_surface_note_2: SITE palette, iteration 4 and the settled one (Rob, 12 Aug): Apple's Human Interface Guidelines system colors, with the Flightline TYPOGRAPHY stack retained (Barlow Condensed / Source Sans 3 / IBM Plex Mono / Bangers) — his explicitly stated exception. sys_* are Apple's published values: grouped backgrounds, hairline separators, systemBlue as the single accent, semantic red/orange/green. History: cream+white (bad, print-as-app), gray workbench (rejected), blue-light (superseded), Apple HIG (current). sys_dim is darkened from Apple's #8A8A8E to hold WCAG AA on white — the one deliberate deviation, recorded here. DOCUMENTS are untouched: kneeboard/brief/guide keep Flightline paper+navy; HIG governs applications, not print.
_surface_note: workbench/well are SCREEN-ONLY surfaces, straight from the kit's own specimen (its body is #D7D8D4 gray with a white page on top). PAPER (#F4F0E6) is a PRINT surface: one page, one ground — used by the kneeboard/brief/guide and never as an app background. The v1.57.0 light mode made that mistake (cream page + white panels + beige cards = three near-whites, no edges) and Rob called it immediately.

semantics._comment: The rules, not just the values. Red is danger/warning/destructive ONLY. Amber is caution/degraded ONLY. Navy is identity, navigation and notes. Every color-coded state carries a text label and, on screens, a shape symbol (WARNING triangle, CAUTION diamond, NORMAL disc).

fonts._comment: Vendored OFL files under fonts/. VF = variable font; weight is set per-use via set_variation_by_axes. DejaVu remains the hard fallback so a missing file degrades a document, never fails a build.

identity_rail._comment: Replaces the v1.55.0 classification banner (the kit explicitly warns against imitating classification markings). Answers: what publication, what subject, what revision, where am I.

_surface_note_3: LIBRARY role taxonomy (v1.61.0, Rob: 'the library colors don't seem to match what would be supported by the Apple HIG'): the seven role_* pairs are Apple's system colors in their HIG ACCESSIBLE variants — cyan(a2a) orange(strike) indigo(sead) brown(cas, the mud-movers) teal(carrier) green(training) purple(historic) — because role labels render as 11px text, where the default system colors fail WCAG AA (systemOrange on white is 2.2:1). Light values are darkened a further step where Apple's accessible value still missed 4.5:1 on sys_fill (a2a/strike/carrier/training); sead_dark is brightened one step for the same reason on sys_dark_fill. Red stays banned from taxonomy (danger only). The teal-as-library-accent era ended here too: the Library's accent is systemBlue like everywhere else; role_carrier speaks only for the carrier ROLE.
_surface_note_4: WCAG pass (v1.63.0): sys_blue at #007AFF is 4.02:1 on white — legal only for large/bold text, but the site set it on 10-13px labels and chips. sys_blue_access (#0040DD, Apple's published accessible-blue) is the SMALL-TEXT accent and the solid-surface fill in light mode; sys_blue_access_dark (#409CFF) is the night small-text accent; sys_blue_solid_dark (#0070E0) is the night solid surface (white text 4.78:1 — Apple's #0A84FF is 3.65 and fails). sys_dim darkened a second step (#6E6E73 -> #69696E) to hold 4.5 on sys_fill, the darkest light surface it sits on. sys_green_access covers small green text (FREE tags, kit checkmarks). --accent (#007AFF) remains for borders, focus rings and icons, where the 3:1 non-text floor applies and passes.
